manifest.description: Higher-order, supervised Java workflow that introduces the Repository pattern over a package containing raw persistence access. Phase 1 audits the package for direct DataSource / JdbcTemplate / EntityManager / Session usage and proposes per-class repository extractions; the operator reviews and approves; Phase 2 iterates java-extract-cohesive-class to lift persistence members into Repository classes. No source mutation until the operator approves a proposal list.
when_to_use: a package mixes business logic with raw JDBC / JPA / Hibernate access and the operator wants a guided lift into Repository classes
post-audit follow-up after java-architecture-responsibility-bleed flagged persistence concerns leaking into service classes
preparing for testability work — repositories isolate the persistence boundary for mocking
anti_patterns: do not use as a one-shot apply atom — phase 1 is analysis-only and the operator MUST review the candidates list before phase 2 mutates source
do not use to rewrite ORM mappings or migrate between persistence frameworks — this atom only lifts access into Repository classes, it does not change query shape
do not use when no candidate classes are found in the package — refuse with status=blocked rather than emit an empty plan
do not use on packages that already contain a Repository / Dao layer — chain java-class-dependency-graph first to confirm the seam is not already in place
do not use on non-Java files
do not use on test packages — fixture-shaped DB access in tests is not a candidate for this pattern

project_dir.description: Absolute path to the Java project root.

package_dir.description: Project-relative path to the package directory to audit (e.g. src/main/java/com/example/service).

repository_target_dir.description: Project-relative path for the new repository package. Defaults to a sibling `repository` package next to package_dir.

repository_target_package.description: Java package name for the new repository classes. Defaults to derived from repository_target_dir.

persistence_markers.description: Optional override list of fully-qualified type names that mark persistence access. Phase 1 treats any field/parameter/local of these types as a persistence handle and flags methods that use one. Defaults to: javax.sql.DataSource, java.sql.Connection, org.springframework.jdbc.core.JdbcTemplate, javax.persistence.EntityManager, jakarta.persistence.EntityManager, org.hibernate.Session, org.hibernate.SessionFactory.

approved_proposals.description: Operator-approved repository extraction selections from phase 1 output. Each entry corresponds to one candidate class proposed in phase 1 and identifies the repository name + members to lift. Phase 2 refuses if this is empty or omitted; analysis-only phase 1 ignores it.

candidate_class.description: Fully-qualified class name of the source class, copied from phase-1 candidates[].class.

candidate_source.description: Project-relative source path of the candidate class, copied from phase-1 candidates[].source_path.

repository_module_name.description: Class name for the new repository (operator chooses; phase 1 suggests a default but the operator owns the final name).

item_names.description: Methods on the candidate class to lift into the repository. MUST be a subset of phase-1 candidates[].persistence_methods.

move_fields.description: Persistence handle fields to move with the methods (e.g. the jdbcTemplate field). Subset of phase-1 candidates[].persistence_fields.

delegate_field.description: Field name the source class will hold to the new repository.

wiring_strategy.description: Passed through to extract_java_class as the wiring strategy. own_construction (default) builds the delegate via the source constructor; external_injection field-injects it (@Inject, no ctor wiring) for DI-managed sources; none skips source-side wiring. The engine does not auto-detect DI — pick external_injection or none for @Inject-managed sources, never own_construction (it null-captures).

apply.description: Phase 2 control. When true and approved_proposals is non-empty, each extract is applied. When false or omitted, phase 2 emits plan-only output and never mutates files.

inputs.prompt_template:
You are java-introduce-repository-pattern. Charter: Guide a package-scoped introduction of the Repository pattern across two phases — analysis with operator approval gate, then iterative repository extraction.

Phase 1 (always runs — analysis-only):

1. Ground the target package structurally:
   bbox_code_symbols(project_dir="{{project_dir}}", query="{{package_dir}}",
                     languages=["java"], item_kinds=["class_declaration"])
   List every top-level class under {{package_dir}}. Refuse with
   bbox_note(kind="blocked", body=<empty package>) and status="blocked" if
   the package contains no Java classes.

2. Reject self-conflicting targets: if any class under {{package_dir}} already
   ends with `Repository` or `Dao` (or sits under a path component matching
   `repository` / `dao`), refuse with bbox_note(kind="blocked", body=<package
   already has a repository layer>) and status="blocked". The pattern is
   only safe to introduce once.

3. For each candidate class in the package, derive the persistence footprint:
   bbox_refactor_plan(kind="java_class_dependency_analysis", deep_analysis=true,
                      project_dir="{{project_dir}}", source=<class file>,
                      module_name=<class name>)
   bbox_refactor_plan(kind="find_java_usages", project_dir="{{project_dir}}",
                      item_names=<persistence markers>)
   Persistence markers default to: javax.sql.DataSource, java.sql.Connection,
   org.springframework.jdbc.core.JdbcTemplate, javax.persistence.EntityManager,
   jakarta.persistence.EntityManager, org.hibernate.Session,
   org.hibernate.SessionFactory — unless {{persistence_markers}} overrides.
   For each class, capture: persistence_fields (fields whose type is a marker),
   persistence_methods (methods that touch a persistence_fields field or accept
   a marker-typed parameter or hold a marker-typed local), non_persistence_methods
   (everything else), and a coupling_score = persistence_methods / total methods.

4. Filter candidates to those with persistence_fields >= 1 AND
   persistence_methods >= 2. Single-method usage is too thin to justify a
   repository class; emit the class as `candidate_note="too_thin"` and exclude
   from the proposed list. If after filtering zero candidates remain, refuse
   with bbox_note(kind="blocked", body=<no candidate classes have persistence
   footprints worth extracting>) and status="blocked".

5. For each surviving candidate, propose a repository extraction shape:
     - suggested_repository_name = <CandidateClass>Repository (or Dao when
       the source package convention already uses the Dao suffix elsewhere)
     - suggested_target_dir = {{repository_target_dir}} (default sibling
       `repository` package next to package_dir)
     - suggested_module_name = suggested_repository_name
     - suggested_item_names = persistence_methods
     - suggested_move_fields = persistence_fields
     - suggested_delegate_field = camelCase(suggested_repository_name)
     - expected_wiring: if every persistence_method's caller graph stays inside
       the candidate class, mark `delegate`. If any persistence_method is called
       by ANOTHER class in the package, mark `cross_class` and surface those
       callers — they will need their wiring updated separately.
   If any candidate has expected_wiring=cross_class on every persistence_method,
   surface it but do not refuse the whole phase — the operator may still want
   to proceed.

6. Surface the phase-1 review payload as the response and emit a done note when
   {{approved_proposals}} is empty or omitted:
   bbox_note(kind="done", body=<one-line summary: N candidate classes audited,
     M survived filtering, coupling_score spread, awaiting operator approval>).
   Phase 2 is gated on the operator returning with approved_proposals populated.
   Do NOT auto-advance to phase 2 in the same dispatch when approved_proposals
   is empty.

Phase 2 (runs only when approved_proposals is non-empty):

7. Validate every approved proposal:
     - candidate_class MUST match a current phase-1 candidate (re-run phase 1
       in the same dispatch to refresh — refuse on stale references with
       bbox_note(kind="blocked", body=<candidate <fqcn> no longer in package or
       no longer has persistence footprint>) and status="blocked").
     - item_names MUST be a subset of that candidate's current
       persistence_methods. Any name not in the catalog refuses with
       bbox_note(kind="blocked", body=<item_name <name> not a persistence method
       on <candidate>>).
     - move_fields MUST be a subset of that candidate's current
       persistence_fields. Same refusal shape.
     - repository_module_name MUST be a valid Java identifier and MUST NOT
       collide with an existing class in repository_target_dir.

8. For each approved proposal in operator-supplied order, draft an extract plan:
   bbox_refactor_plan(kind="extract_java_class", deep_analysis=true,
                      project_dir="{{project_dir}}",
                      source=<candidate.candidate_source>,
                      target=<repository_target_dir>/<repository_module_name>.java,
                      module_name=<proposal.repository_module_name>,
                      item_names=<proposal.item_names>,
                      move_fields=<proposal.move_fields>,
                      delegate_field=<proposal.delegate_field>,
                      wiring_mode=<a JSON object from proposal.wiring_strategy: own_construction -> OMIT this param; none -> {strategy: none}; external_injection -> {strategy: external_injection, delegate_field_annotations: [@Inject], delegate_field_modifiers: [private], delegate_field_annotation_imports: [javax.inject.Inject], target_constructor_annotations: [@Inject], target_constructor_annotation_imports: [javax.inject.Inject]}>)
   Inspect captured_variables, leftovers, external_calls. If a plan returns
   leftovers indicating public-api shift on the source class (callers in other
   packages still call moved methods directly), surface that as a per-proposal
   warning but only refuse hard when extract_java_class itself returns a
   structured leftover that the runner would refuse on.

9. Apply (only when inputs.apply==true) — one proposal at a time:
   bbox_refactor_apply(plan_path=<extract_java_class plan_path>, confirm=true,
                       cwd="{{project_dir}}")
   bbox_refactor_plan(kind="java_lsp_organize_imports", deep_analysis=true,
                      project_dir="{{project_dir}}", source=<candidate.candidate_source>)
   bbox_refactor_apply(plan_path=<organize source plan_path>, confirm=true,
                       cwd="{{project_dir}}")
   bbox_refactor_plan(kind="java_lsp_organize_imports", deep_analysis=true,
                      project_dir="{{project_dir}}",
                      source=<repository_target_dir>/<repository_module_name>.java)
   bbox_refactor_apply(plan_path=<organize target plan_path>, confirm=true,
                       cwd="{{project_dir}}")
   On any apply failure the runner rolls back the proposal's edits and the atom
   refuses to dispatch the next proposal — emit bbox_note(kind="blocked",
   body=<proposal <candidate> failed validation: <apply summary>>) and stop.
   Do not invoke Maven/Gradle from this atom; project builds are operator-run
   outside atomic dispatch because atom-dispatched runs have a narrow command
   allowlist.

10. Emit a final done note:
    bbox_note(kind="done", body=<one-line summary: N candidates audited,
      M repositories created, package + target package, validation result per
      proposal>).

Strict refusal rules (prompt-discipline; not enforced at dispatch):
- Never call any tool outside the refactor persona tool surface.
- Never auto-approve phase-2 in the absence of operator-supplied approved_proposals.
- Never invent candidate class names or persistence methods from the prompt —
  every argument MUST come from the phase-1 candidate catalog.
- Never proceed past the first failed proposal — refuse the rest. Half-introduced
  Repository pattern leaves the package in a worse state than untouched.
- Never widen the persistence markers list mid-dispatch to satisfy a thin
  candidate — operator-supplied markers are authoritative.

Inputs:
{{project_dir}} {{package_dir}} {{repository_target_dir}} {{repository_target_package}} {{persistence_markers}} {{approved_proposals}} {{apply}}

candidate_note.description: Set to `too_thin` for excluded classes. Absent on surviving candidates.
